description: Use of property as live/work unit (Use Class Sui Generis) comprising art studio/gallery at ground floor with residential to the upper floors; associated internal and external alterations including restorations to the front elevation; erection of a mansard roof extension; and demolition of exiting and construction of a new outbuilding in the rear garden.
decision_conditions: <p>The floorspace shown in hatched with purple outline and labelled “Studio / Gallery” shall be retained and used solely for commercial purposes within Use Class E and the area shown in hatched with green outline and labelled "residential" shall be retained and used solely for residential purposes within Use Class C3 and for no other purpose, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.</p><p>The commercial floorspace shall not be incorporated into the residential accommodation at any time.</p><p>REASON: To ensure the retention of the commercial element of the approved live/work unit, to maintain an active frontage and mixed use character of the area.</p>

The Development hereby permitted shall only be carried out and completed strictly in accordance with the submitted plans hereby approved and any subsequent approval of details.


REASON: To ensure that the development hereby permitted is carried out in full accordance with the plans hereby approved.

<p>Prior to superstructure works, a detailed specification, drainage layout and management and maintenance plan for at least one suitable sustainable drainage system (e.g. water butt with overflow, raingarden, bioretention planter box, living roof with 80–150mm substrate, permeable paving) shall be submitted to and approved by the LPA in consultation with the LLFA.</p><p>If soakaways are used, infiltration testing must demonstrate soil capacity. It must be shown that there will be no increase in surface water discharge off-site and that peak flow rate and volume are reduced.</p><p>REASON: To ensure appropriate surface water management in accordance with London Plan and Local Plan policy.</p>

<p>The protective fencing shall be 2.4m high and conform to Figure 2 of BS 5837:2012. Temporary ground protection shall be used where construction access is required within the RPA, selected in accordance with the loading of anticipated traffic:</p><p>a) Pedestrian only: Scaffold boards over a scaffold frame or over 100mm woodchip on geotextile membrane</p><p>b) Pedestrian-operated plant (up to 2t): Inter-linked protection boards over 150mm woodchip on geotextile membrane</p><p>c) Vehicles over 2t: Engineered ground protection system or reinforced concrete slabs designed with arboricultural input</p><p>REASON: To protect the long-term health of trees under Section 197(a) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 and ensure no compaction or damage to root systems.</p>

<p>All new underground utilities including drainage must be routed outside the RPAs unless otherwise agreed. Where routing within RPAs is unavoidable, trenchless methods (BS5837:2012 Table 3) must be used, with pits located outside the RPA.</p><p>REASON: To safeguard existing trees and prevent long-term harm to roots and soil hydrology, in accordance with LP51.</p>

The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

<p>No development shall take place until a detailed Demolition and Construction Management Plan covering the matters set out below has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall only be implemented in accordance with the details and measures approved as part of the demolition and construction management plan, which shall be maintained throughout the entire construction period.</p><p>● A demolition and construction method statement covering all phases of the development to include details of noise control measures and measures to preserve air quality (including a risk assessment of the demolition and construction phase);</p><p>● A demolition and construction waste management plan setting out how resources will be managed and waste controlled at all stages during a construction project, including, but not limited to, details of dust mitigation measures during construction works, the location of any mobile plant machinery, details of measures to be employed to mitigate against noise and vibration arising out of the construction process demonstrating best practical means;</p><p>● A demolition and construction traffic management plan to include the following: the construction programme/timescales; the number/frequency and size of construction vehicles; construction traffic route and trip generation; location of deliveries; pedestrian and vehicular access arrangements; any temporary road/footway closures during the construction period; details of parking suspensions (if required) and the duration of construction;</p><p>● A dust management plan to include details of how dust from construction activity will be controlled / mitigated against following best practice guidance. This should include monitoring of particulate matter at the application site boundary in the direction of sensitive receptors following the SPG Mayor of London Control of Dust and Emissions Guidance.</p><p>REASON: To avoid hazard and obstruction being caused to users of the public highway and in the interest of public safety and amenity. To protect air quality and people’s health by ensuring that the production of air pollutants, such as nitrogen dioxide and particulate matter, are kept to a minimum during the course of building works.</p>

<p>The following elements of the scheme shall not be installed, implemented or carried out unless in accordance with details which shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The works shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details.</p><p>a) External materials, including any reclaimed brick</p><p>b) Details of proposed rooflight including manufacturer’s details and 1:5 scale cross section drawing</p><p>c) Details of proposed front door to shop</p><p>d) Details of proposed staircase</p><p>REASON: To ensure that special regard is paid to protecting the special architectural and historic interest and integrity of the building under Sections 16 and 66 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990; the NPPF; the London Plan Policy HC1; and Hackney Local Plan Policies LP1, LP3 and LP4.</p>

<p>The live/work unit hereby approved shall operate in strict accordance with approved drawing 'Site, Showing Uses (No. 816/25P001 (02.2026))' and for no other purpose. The commercial floorspace shall not be incorporated into the residential accommodation at any time.</p><p>REASON: To ensure the retention of the commercial element of the approved live/work unit, to maintain an active frontage and mixed use character of the area.</p>

<p>Prior to occupation, full soft landscaping details shall be submitted and approved, including:</p><p>● A tree planting plan following the 10-20-30 species/genus/family diversity rule</p><p>● Soil volumes</p><p>● Projected mature height and canopy spread</p><p>● Tree pit and planter specifications</p><p>● Methods of support and protection</p><p>● A varied plant structure including native species, flowering plants and evergreen species</p><p>● A diverse distribution of plants</p><p>● A management and maintenance plan (watering, mulching, weeding, young tree care, removal of ties/stakes, monitoring, replacement of failures)</p><p>● A detailed planting plan showing species, sizes, age, numbers and planting locations</p><p>● Details of grassed or turfed areas</p><p>Any tree that dies or becomes damaged within 5 years shall be replaced in the following planting season.</p><p>All approved landscaping shall be implemented within the first planting season following completion and maintained for 10 years.</p><p>REASON: To ensure the development enhances biodiversity, in accordance with LP47 and LP51 of the Hackney Local Plan and the NPPF.</p>
